text:
Aisha: FYI seeing a burst of ScheduleFailed on gpu pods in us-west-2 after the nightly jobs kicked off. lots of "0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" errors.
Miguel: ugh. is this the batch workload that requests 2 gpus each? we recently moved it to the new gpu-heavy pool.
Aisha: yep, the batch worker requests 2 GPUs and 32Gi memory. previously clustered differently so packing worked. now nodes are 4xGPU (A100-40), but pods are getting fragmented across nodes so autoscaler isn't adding the right mix.
Priya: can you paste `kubectl describe pod` for one of the failing pods? curious if tolerations/taints are blocking packing.
Aisha: pasted below:
```
Name:           batch-worker-7fc9b
Namespace:      ml-batch
Priority:       0
Node-Selector:  accelerator=nvidia
Tolerations:    <none>
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient memory, 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Miguel: autoscaler logs show it scaled up one node in gpu-heavy but then another pod got scheduled and the attempted packing still left 2 GPUs unused on multiple nodes. scale-up target was 1 node, but binpacking would need different node sizes.
k8s-autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp: candidate group: nodegroup/gpu-heavy-e2, estimated 1 node(s) to add. (timestamp: 1768001290)
Priya: we have three levers here: reduce per-pod gpu request (if app supports multi-process on 1 GPU), enable MIG fractional GPUs on a MIG-enabled nodepool, or change node pool shapes (e.g., 8x -> 2x GPU nodes) so packing fits.
Miguel: can we create a small nodepool with 1xGPU instances and move this workload there? cheaper to pack but increases cluster count.
Aisha: wanted to avoid extra nodepools — ops prefers to use single gpu-heavy pool. but packing poor because pods request 2 GPUs (must be integer) and k8s device plugin allocates full devices.
Priya: another option: run a lightweight packing controller that sets pod.resourceRequests.gpu to 1 when possible or run a sidecar to multiplex. but that's more invasive. Short term patch: change the deployment to request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and increase replicas from 4 -> 8 to keep throughput.
Miguel: agree. also test enabling `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` in cluster-autoscaler? our heterogeneous pools are confusing the CA's scale-up choice.
SRE Oncall: have we checked kube-scheduler metrics? if scheduler is using generic-scheduler plugin for resource binpacking we could prefer `BinPack` priority.
Aisha: ran a quick patch to one deployment to request 1 GPU and bumped replicas, pods scheduled immediately onto existing nodes.
Priya: nice. for longer term we should:
- add a MIG-enabled nodepool for fractional workloads
- update autoscaler config to prefer scaling the 1xGPU pool for this namespace
- add a simple alert for high GPU fragmentation (ratio of idle GPUs across nodes > 0.5)
Miguel: I'll open a PR to add the 1xGPU nodepool and a CA scale-target annotation we can use: `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-to` on the namespace.
Aisha: thanks — for now the hotfix patch is in prod (deploy-bot: deploy/cluster: batch-worker@sha256:abc123). :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment batch-worker scaled to 8 replicas (hash: abc123).
k8s-autoscaler-bot: scaleComplete: nodegroup/gpu-heavy-e2 increased by 1 (now 5 nodes) (timestamp: 1768001400).
Priya: follow-up: can someone run a quick binpacking sim with our daily workload profile? I can provide the pod size distribution.
Miguel: on it — will run simulation and post results in a follow-up thread.
Aisha: closing this thread once CA change + 1xGPU pool PR is merged. thanks everyone. :rocket:
